text:
David Pastrnak has become the Bruins' answer to a bad night. 98.5 The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson counted seven goals and 13 points in eight games after a loss this season, and the captain did it again on Nov. 18 in Detroit, with a goal and an assist to end a three-game skid. He has 31 points in 23 games (11 goals, 20 assists), with a 7-5 win over Washington on Saturday adding three more.

Our numbers like most of it. His finishing is honest, 11 goals on 9.2 expected, and Boston has 56% of 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice. The soft spot is the assists: the Bruins have scored 5.6 more goals than their chances deserve while he's out there, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. The New York Times also singled out his turnovers in a recent stats column. Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best with weaker help last season, which makes his raw numbers look worse than his own effect. Our numbers project about 106 points.
headline: David Pastrnak is Boston's answer to a bad night
